OSKAR [SURNAME]
Senior Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [PORTFOLIO / GITHUB]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior software developer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications. Strongest in frontend development with React and TypeScript, alongside professional experience building Node.js services with NestJS and working with PostgreSQL. Has delivered onboarding features, led development of a mobile ticketing app with approximately 50,000 downloads, and served as acting team lead for four months.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, Angular, React Native
Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express, Laravel
Databases and data: PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma
Cloud and services: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS; Firebase Cloud Messaging
Other: WordPress, GraphQL (Apollo Server; maintenance of a BFF), Terraform (small edits), Python (basic), YAML

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Fullstack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | 2021–Present
- Build onboarding features for a fintech product using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS.
- Implemented a Swedish BankID identity verification step with QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK.
- A/B tested the identity step on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Built a secure document-upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, SQS status updates and PostgreSQL.
- Contributed to the incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, route by route, behind the same API gateway.
- Acted as team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead’s parental leave, including one-to-ones and sprint planning.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | 2018–2021
- Delivered client web and mobile projects using Angular, React, React Native, Laravel and WordPress.
- Served as project tech lead for a two-developer React Native ferry-ticket app, building most of the app; the other developer handled the payment backend.

Developer | Nordkust Media | 2014–2018
- Worked on newspaper websites.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Ferry Ticket Mobile App | Sjöbris Digital for a ferry operator | 2019–2020
- Built most of a React Native app for buying and displaying ferry tickets offline; the app has approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Technologies: React Native, TypeScript, Node.js, Firebase Cloud Messaging.

BankID Identity Verification Flow | Älvgrind Fintech | 2022
- Delivered a new onboarding identity step supporting Swedish BankID QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS.

Secure Document Upload | Älvgrind Fintech | 2023
- Implemented document uploads up to 20 MB using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, and SQS scan-status updates into PostgreSQL.
- Technologies: AWS S3, Lambda, SQS, NestJS, PostgreSQL.

Express to NestJS Migration | Älvgrind Fintech | 2021–2022
- Contributed to an incremental onboarding-backend migration from Express to NestJS, keeping routes behind the same API gateway during the migration.
- Gave a meetup talk about the migration in 2022.
- Technologies: Node.js, Express, NestJS, TypeORM, Prisma.

PERSONAL PROJECTS

Home Assistant Integrations | 2022–Present
- Created two small custom home-automation integrations, published on GitHub with approximately 40 stars combined.
- Technologies: Python (basic), YAML.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, readable technical CV with a clear senior full-stack/frontend positioning, credible career progression, and several high-impact quantified achievements. The BankID conversion improvement, 50,000-download mobile app, secure document-upload flow, and acting team-lead experience are particularly persuasive. The main content weakness is incompleteness against this specific role: the CV does not address testing, Git workflows, accessibility, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, English proficiency, or privacy/security awareness explicitly. The repeated detail in Selected Projects largely duplicates the Professional Experience section, while the Nordkust Media role is unusually sparse. The unresolved contact placeholders also make the document appear unfinished.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, plain text bullets, and recognizable technology keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, Express, A/B testing, and S3. Parsing and keyword matching should therefore be generally strong, with a moderate-to-high AI screening probability for the core React/TypeScript/Node/PostgreSQL profile. ATS relevance would improve by adding explicit, truthful terms for the requirements that are supported by the candidate's material, especially English proficiency, authentication/identity verification, web security, and Git only if documented elsewhere. The slash in the headline is acceptable, but a single target title such as "Senior Full-Stack Engineer | TypeScript / React" would be slightly clearer. The bracketed placeholders for name, email, phone, LinkedIn, and portfolio/GitHub must be completed before submission.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the core engineering stack: the CV clearly demonstrates more than two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, AWS, and A/B testing. The fintech context and BankID/document-upload work also provide relevant evidence of identity verification, sensitive-data handling, and security-conscious engineering. The mobile ticketing project supports the product-focused and user-impact aspects of the role, and the acting team-lead experience is relevant to collaboration and mentoring potential. However, the CV does not demonstrate semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility/WCAG, automated unit/integration/end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP Top 10 awareness, health-data privacy, Next.js/SSR, Docker, design systems/Storybook, German/Croatian, or healthcare experience. These are candidate-profile gaps or unverified areas rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting, so they should not be claimed without supporting evidence. The A/B-testing requirement is already well supported.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. Before submission, replace every unresolved placeholder in the header—"OSKAR [SURNAME]", "[EMAIL]", "[PHONE]", "[LINKEDIN]", and "[PORTFOLIO / GITHUB]"—with the candidate's real details. If no portfolio link is intended, remove that placeholder rather than leaving it in the document.
2. In the headline, change "Senior Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer" to "Senior Full-Stack Engineer | TypeScript / React". This preserves the candidate's frontend strength while matching the advertised title and primary technologies more directly.
3. In the Professional Summary, replace the current summary with a tighter role-targeted version that retains only supported claims, for example: "Senior full-stack engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications. Strongest in React and TypeScript, with professional experience developing Node.js services using NestJS and Express and working with PostgreSQL and AWS. Delivered onboarding and identity-verification features, increased onboarding conversion from 61% to 74% through A/B testing, and built a React Native ticketing app with approximately 50,000 downloads. Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024." Do not add accessibility, testing, healthcare, or privacy claims unless supported by the candidate's actual experience.
4. Add a concise Languages section after Technical Skills. State the candidate's accurate English proficiency level; the source material demonstrates that the candidate can write in English, but the CV should not label English as "fluent" unless that is accurate.

MEANINGFUL ENHANCEMENTS:
5. In Technical Skills, reorder the categories so the most relevant keywords appear first: "Frontend: React, TypeScript, Angular, React Native"; "Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express"; "Databases: PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma"; and "Cloud and services: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS, Firebase Cloud Messaging." Keep Laravel, WordPress, GraphQL, Terraform, Python, and YAML in a separate "Additional Technologies" line so the primary match is immediately visible.
6. In the Älvgrind Fintech AB experience section, revise the first bullet to make the end-to-end scope and advertised technologies explicit: "Build patient/customer-facing-style onboarding features using React and TypeScript, with Node.js/NestJS services, PostgreSQL, and AWS." Retain the existing fintech wording if "patient/customer-facing-style" would be inaccurate; do not imply healthcare experience.
7. In the same Älvgrind section, revise the BankID bullet to use the supported security terminology without overclaiming: "Implemented a Swedish BankID identity-verification flow with QR-code and same-device authentication journeys through a provider SDK." This makes the authentication relevance clearer while remaining faithful to the source material.
8. In the same section, combine the secure-upload details into an impact-oriented bullet: "Built a secure document-upload flow for files up to 20 MB using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, SQS status updates, and PostgreSQL." This improves keyword matching for secure handling, AWS, asynchronous processing, and SQL without adding unsupported claims.
9. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. Keep the detailed BankID, Secure Document Upload, Express-to-NestJS Migration, and Ferry Ticket Mobile App entries as selected projects, but shorten the corresponding experience bullets to emphasize role scope and outcomes. This will make the CV more concise while preserving the strongest evidence.
10. In the Sjöbris Digital Agency AB section, retain the existing truthful leadership wording but make it more prominent: "Served as project tech lead in a two-developer React Native ferry-ticket app team and built most of the app; the other developer handled the payment backend." Do not imply ownership of the payment backend.
11. In the Nordkust Media section, either add specific responsibilities or outcomes from the candidate's records, or keep the entry as a one-line role without implying technologies or achievements that are not documented. Its current single bullet creates an apparent completeness gap compared with the detailed later roles.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The header contains unresolved placeholders for the candidate's surname and contact/profile links, making the CV appear unfinished and potentially preventing recruiter contact. Fix: replace or remove all bracketed placeholders before submission.
2. No unsupported technologies or experiences were detected when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information. The listed React, TypeScript, Angular, React Native, Node.js, NestJS, Express, Laravel, WordPress, PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma, AWS services, Firebase Cloud Messaging, GraphQL/Apollo Server, Terraform, Python, YAML, BankID, ClamAV, A/B testing, acting team leadership, and meetup talk are supported by the source material.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "Senior Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer"
- "Senior software developer"

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, and professionally focused. The summary communicates seniority, core technologies, domain context, leadership exposure, and strong quantified outcomes. The BankID, document-upload, migration, and ferry-app projects provide useful evidence of delivery impact. However, the document has some avoidable repetition: the BankID project repeats the same identity-verification point in two consecutive bullets, and several project details duplicate the Professional Experience section. The Nordkust Media role is almost empty, and the language line appears unfinished. No contact details or professional links are shown, which weakens practical usability if this is the complete CV.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain section headings, standard reverse-chronological structure, conventional bullets, and explicit technology groupings should parse well in ATS systems. Core matching keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, AWS, authentication/identity verification, A/B testing, and fintech are present. AI/ATS screening probability is good for the core stack and full-stack experience, but only moderate overall because the CV does not evidence several explicit requirements: automated unit/end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, OWASP/security terminology, or fluent English. These should not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience. The use of a vertical bar in the title and slash in the specialty is generally ATS-safe, but standardizing the title to the exact role wording would improve matching slightly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a credible match for the central role: it shows substantially more than the required React/TypeScript experience, Node.js services, SQL databases, AWS, NestJS, fintech work, authentication, secure document handling, and A/B testing. The acting team-lead experience also supports the squad-based and mentoring-oriented environment. The fintech and identity-document work are relevant adjacent experience for a privacy-conscious healthcare product, although healthcare or health-data experience is not shown. The strongest alignment is with the engineering stack, experimentation, and security-adjacent product work. The main candidate-side gaps are accessibility evidence, automated testing, Git workflows, explicit OWASP awareness, Docker, SSR/Next.js, Storybook/design systems, German/Croatian, and confirmed fluent English. These are gaps or unverified areas rather than defects that can be solved by inventing CV content.
critique.improvement_instructions:
HIGH PRIORITY — In the Selected Projects section under “BankID Identity Verification Flow,” remove the duplicated bullet “Implemented a Swedish BankID identity-verification flow with QR-code and same-device authentication journeys through a provider SDK.” Keep the first, more concise version and retain the separate quantified A/B-testing bullet.

HIGH PRIORITY — In the Languages section, remove the unfinished wording “Proficiency level not specified.” Replace it with the candidate’s accurate English level only if the candidate can substantiate that level. Do not label English “fluent” without confirmation.

HIGH PRIORITY — At the top of the CV, add practical contact details that are available, such as email, phone, LinkedIn, and the actual GitHub/portfolio URL for the published Home Assistant integrations. Do not insert placeholder or invented URLs.

MEDIUM PRIORITY — In the Professional Experience section under “Developer | Nordkust Media,” add the supported scope from the candidate information, for example: “Built and maintained newspaper websites and other web projects.” If more detail is unavailable, retain the concise entry rather than inventing technologies or achievements.

MEDIUM PRIORITY — In the Professional Summary, tighten the wording so the role match appears earlier. For example, change the opening to: “Senior full-stack engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications, strongest in React and TypeScript, with Node.js/NestJS, PostgreSQL, and AWS experience.” Keep the conversion and 50,000-download achievements because they are strong evidence.

MINOR — Standardize the job title to the advertised wording where truthful: “Senior Full-Stack Engineer | TypeScript / React.” Also use “Full-Stack” consistently instead of alternating between “Fullstack” and “Full-Stack.”

MINOR — Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects by keeping broad responsibilities in Experience and outcome-heavy technical detail in Projects. For example, retain the conversion result and leadership scope in Experience, while reserving the detailed BankID and AWS implementation details for the project entry.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, and professionally written. It presents a credible 12-year full-stack background, strong React/TypeScript positioning, relevant Node.js/PostgreSQL/AWS experience, and several concrete outcomes. The 61% to 74% conversion improvement, approximately 50,000 app downloads, and acting team-lead experience provide useful evidence of impact. The selected-project format is particularly effective for showing technical depth. The main content weakness is that several requirements from the job description are not evidenced, while the document does not include contact details or links that would normally appear in a complete CV header.

Core matching terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, A/B testing, Express, and React Native are present. ATS matching would improve by using the exact phrase "SQL databases" alongside PostgreSQL and by adding accurate contact, LinkedIn, or GitHub details if available. The document does not claim unsupported testing, Git, accessibility, Docker, Next.js, Storybook, or OWASP experience, which is correct, but this means automated screening may rank it lower for those requirements. AI screening probability is strong for the core React/TypeScript/Node.js/PostgreSQL/AWS profile and moderate overall because several must-have keywords are not supported by the supplied candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a strong match for the core engineering stack: more than two years of professional React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend services, PostgreSQL, AWS, and analytics/A/B testing. The fintech onboarding, BankID identity-verification, and secure document-upload work provides relevant evidence of working with identity, sensitive documents, security-related flows, and a regulated-adjacent product environment. The ferry-ticket app also demonstrates user-facing mobile product delivery and technical leadership. Alignment is weaker or unverified for semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, automated unit/integration/end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP Top 10, health-data privacy, Docker, Next.js/SSR, design systems, and Storybook. German or Croatian is not shown. The CV also does not explicitly establish fluent English, although the candidate's English-language material demonstrates English communication ability. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be solved by adding unsupported claims.
